name: Moxifloxacin 0.5% Eye Drops
dosage: 1 drop in the affected eye(s) 3 to 4 times daily for 7 days. For severe corneal ulcer: 1 drop every 1-2 hours initially under specialist guidance.
contraindications: Do not touch dropper tip to eye or eyelid
warnings: Prolonged use may cause fungal overgrowth. Discontinue if rash or allergic edema appears.
interactions: None significant with systemic meds, space 10 minutes apart from other topical eye drops

name: Timolol Maleate 0.5% Eye Drops
dosage: 1 drop in the affected eye twice daily (approximately 12 hours apart). In acute spikes, administer under clinical supervision.
contraindications: Bronchial asthma or history of COPD
warnings: Systemic absorption occurs via nasolacrimal duct. Punctal occlusion is recommended for 2 minutes post-instillation.

name: Prednisolone Acetate 1% Ophthalmic Suspension
dosage: 1-2 drops into conjunctival sac 2 to 4 times daily. In acute severe inflammation, may be given every 1 hour for first 24-48 hours.
contraindications: Active epithelial Herpes Simplex Keratitis (dendritic ulcer)
warnings: CRITICAL: Do NOT use in suspected viral dendritic ulcer or fungal keratitis. May elevate Intraocular Pressure (IOP) or induce cataracts with prolonged use.
interactions: NSAID eye drops (synergistic delay in epithelial healing)

name: Carboxymethylcellulose 0.5% / 1% Lubricant Eye Drops
dosage: 1 to 2 drops in the affected eye(s) as needed, typically 3 to 6 times daily.
warnings: Remove contact lenses before instillation. Allow 5 minutes between different drops.
side_effects: Mild transient blurriness immediately after drop

name: Atropine Sulfate 1% Ophthalmic Solution
indications: Acute anterior uveitis/iridocyclitis to prevent posterior synechiae and relieve ciliary spasm pain
dosage: 1 drop up to 3 times daily or as directed by ophthalmologist.
contraindications: Narrow-angle glaucoma or anatomically narrow anterior chamber angles
warnings: CRITICAL: Can precipitate acute angle closure glaucoma in predisposed shallow angles! Punctal occlusion is mandatory in pediatric patients.

name: Balanced Salt Solution / Normal Saline 0.9% Sterile Irrigation
indications: Chemical burn of the eye (alkali/acid splash)
dosage: EMERGENCY: Copious continuous irrigation with 1000ml to 2000ml sterile saline or clean tap water immediately for at least 15-30 minutes until neutral pH (7.2-7.4) is reached.
contraindications: Open globe perforation with extrusion of intraocular contents (requires immediate sterile eye shield instead of pressurized jet)
warnings: Do NOT delay irrigation to find specific antidotes! Immediate copious water or saline wash saves corneal transparency.

name: Acetazolamide 250mg Tablets
indications: Acute angle-closure glaucoma attack (rapid IOP reduction)
dosage: Emergency: 500 mg orally as initial dose, followed by 250 mg every 6 hours under strict ophthalmologist supervision.
warnings: Monitor serum electrolytes (potassium). May cause metabolic acidosis in elderly or renal impaired.

name: Paracetamol 500mg / 1000mg
dosage: 500mg to 1000mg orally every 6 to 8 hours as needed. Maximum daily dose 4000mg (4 grams).
contraindications: Severe active hepatic impairment or acute liver failure
warnings: Do not combine with other paracetamol-containing medications to avoid inadvertent hepatotoxicity.
side_effects: Rare allergic reactions, nausea at excessive doses
interactions: Warfarin (high chronic doses may increase INR)

name: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) WHO Formula
indications: Vomiting associated with acute angle glaucoma or systemic illness
dosage: Dissolve 1 sachet in 500ml clean drinking water. Drink small frequent sips continuously as needed.
contraindications: Severe persistent shock or unconscious patient (requires immediate IV fluids)
warnings: Always use correct volume of potable water (do not make too concentrated).
side_effects: Mild hypernatremia if consumed inappropriately in excessive concentration

name: Amlodipine 5mg / 10mg
indications: Hypertensive emergency adjunct after physician evaluation
dosage: Initial dose 5mg once daily, titrate to 10mg once daily under physician guidance.
warnings: Do not stop abruptly. Monitor peripheral ankle edema.
